items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: school was such an incredible experience for me, Eastman, an absolutely incredible experience. To play one day in a brass quintet, to play the next day in a symphony, to play the next day a recital with somebody.

ctx.x: Do you regret not finishing college at all?

Well at this point I don’t see what the specific degree I would have gotten, a bachelor’s in performance, I mean I don’t know what that would do for me in my life right now. My mother died of cancer about two and a half years ago and on her death bed she still was ranting and raving about wanting me to get a degree. But I hope that she understands and I think, Mom I’m not starving, I’m fine. And I still see what taking the time out to do that, what I’ve done and what — school was such an incredible experience for…

because I was big, I don’t know. And then jingles I was already starting to do while I was in college. So I was starting to work already in college, constantly practicing. I was the first person in practice in the morning, the last one to leave. The guard was like okay there’s Byron, I’ve got to kick Byron out of the practice room, it’s eleven o’clock, he knows it closes at eleven, I’ve got to kick him out again. You know I was the first and last always. So the experience of being in school was an incredible…
